facebook.content_angle: Turns in the pool — how most club swimmers lose 1–2 seconds per lap at the wall through a weak, slow flip turn, and the three-step drill to fix it fast
facebook.post_text:
Your flip turn is costing you more time than your stroke ever will. 🚨

Most club swimmers train hard in the water, then give it all back at the wall. A slow, sloppy turn can bleed 1–2 seconds per lap — that's 30+ seconds over a 1500m race before you've even taken a stroke.

Here's where it breaks down:
👉 Approaching the wall too slow — you're decelerating 3–4 strokes out instead of carrying speed into the turn
👉 Tucking too late — your rotation is sluggish because you haven't timed the somersault to your stroke count
👉 Planting your feet too low on the wall — you push outward, not forward, and lose your streamline angle immediately

Elite swimmers don't just swim faster — they turn faster. ⚡

Fix it with this three-step drill:
✔️ Count your strokes to the wall every rep until the approach becomes automatic
✔️ Practice explosive turns off the wall with a coach watching your foot placement — aim for shoulder height
✔️ Hold a tight streamline for a full three seconds post-push before your first stroke

How many laps do you swim per session? Multiply that by 2 seconds — that's the time sitting on the table.
